original_question: Let M be a sigma-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold of dimension n > 0, let p be a point of M, and let Diff_c(M)_{p,0} be the subgroup of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms fixing p whose tangent map at p has positive determinant. Is every formal diffeomorphism of R^n whose linear part has positive determinant realized as the Taylor series at p of some element of Diff_c(M)_{p,0}? Equivalently, is the Taylor-series homomorphism T_p^infinity: Diff_c(M)_{p,0} -> G^n_f(R)_0 surjective?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1, together with its equivalent reformulation in Proposition 1.2 and its affirmative resolution in Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft is already aimed at the paper’s exact Borel-type problem: a σ-compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold M, a point p in M, compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms fixing p, the positivity condition on the determinant of the tangent map at p, realization of a prescribed formal local diffeomorphism as a Taylor series at p, and the equivalent surjectivity question for the Taylor-series homomorphism.
missing_details: The paper formulates the local object as a formal diffeomorphism in local coordinates at p, i.e. an invertible n-tuple of formal power series in R[[x_1,…,x_n]] fixing 0, not just informally as a formal diffeomorphism of R^n.
The subgroup G_f^n(R)_0 should be defined explicitly as the subgroup of the formal diffeomorphism group whose linear part lies in GL_n^+(R), equivalently has positive determinant.
The Taylor series at p is taken after choosing a local chart around p with chart value 0; Proposition 1.2 is what makes the surjectivity formulation the chart-independent equivalent version.
Diff_c(M)_{p,0} should be spelled out as the subgroup of Diff_c(M) consisting of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms φ with φ(p)=p and det(T_pφ)>0.
The dimension variable should be tied explicitly to the target formal group: n = dim(M) > 0.
To stay paper-faithful, the question should be posed as the exact realization problem from Conjecture 1.1, with the surjectivity statement only as the equivalent formulation from Proposition 1.2.
refined_question: Let M be a σ-compact smooth manifold over R of dimension n > 0, let p be a point of M, and choose a smooth chart κ: U → V ⊂ R^n with κ(p)=0. If F=(F_1,…,F_n) is a formal diffeomorphism at 0, i.e. an invertible n-tuple of formal power series in R[[x_1,…,x_n]] with F(0)=0 and det(D_0F)>0, does there exist a compactly supported C∞-diffeomorphism φ of M such that φ(p)=p, det(T_pφ)>0, and the formal Taylor series of κ∘φ∘κ^{-1} at 0 is exactly F?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, with Diff_c(M)_{p,0} = {φ in Diff_c(M) : φ(p)=p and det(T_pφ)>0} and G_f^n(R)_0 the group of formal diffeomorphisms of R^n at 0 whose linear part has positive determinant, is the Taylor-series homomorphism T_p^∞: Diff_c(M)_{p,0} → G_f^n(R)_0 surjective?
justification: The draft is not drifting to a neighboring problem: it matches the paper’s Borel-type realization question for compactly supported diffeomorphisms. In Section 1 this is introduced as Conjecture 1.1; Proposition 1.2 gives exactly the surjectivity reformulation via the Taylor-series homomorphism; and Theorem 1.3 states that the conjecture is true. The abstract independently summarizes the same result as the existence of compactly supported smooth diffeomorphisms with prescribed Taylor series around p, under the positive-determinant condition.
